messages:
deploy-bot: scheduled migration v2026_03_24_split_user_metadata at 1769350200. staggered_shards=4, auto-canary=manual. pin recommended for non-idempotent steps. :calendar:

marta: quick summary: splitting user.metadata JSON into new normalized table user_metadata. steps: 1) add table + FK (fast) 2) backfill rows from JSON -> new table in batches 3) swap read path via feature flag 4) drop old column.

kevin: important: backfill will touch large partitions (shard 2 and 3). need cross-region replica check for eu-west we saw 15s lag last week. prefer running shard pilot on us-east only first.

sre-lead: agree. set pilot_shards=[0] for canary. also schedule the window to start at 2026-03-24 01:00 UTC (local midnight PST). verify on-call rotation covers that slot.

deploy-bot: pin applied -> pinned_version = v2026_03_24_split_user_metadata. holdpoint set at post-backfill-check.

marta: backfill plan: single-writer per shard, limit 5k, sleep 2000ms, checkpoint on last_id. use checksum per batch to validate counts. psuedocode:

```sql
-- pseudo backfill for a shard
WITH to_move AS (
  SELECT id, metadata FROM users WHERE metadata IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 5000
)
INSERT INTO user_metadata (user_id, key, value)
SELECT id, k, v FROM to_move, json_each_text(to_move.metadata) as (k,v);
DELETE FROM users_metadata_tmp WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM to_move);
-- record last id checkpoint
```

kevin: minor tweak: avoid json_each_text on primary; stream parsing in app worker to reduce DB CPU. also set statement_timeout=60s for the insert connection to avoid long locks.

product-bot: product ok with rolling feature flag. will only flip for 5% of users after shard waves 1-2 look nominal. include release-note snippet: "Normalized user metadata table. Pilot by shard; rollbackable."

sre-lead: rollback triggers: if error_rate > 0.5% for 15m OR replication_lag > 20s OR sustained lock_waits > 5/min -> abort and run revert. revert script location: s3://redwood-backups/reverts/revert_v2026_03_24.sql. revert command: `psql -f revert_v2026_03_24.sql --host=write-db-primary`

marta: added checksum step after each shard wave: compare count(user_metadata where created_by_migration) == expected_count. if mismatch -> pause and investigate.

oncall-bot: REMINDER: canary pilot (shard 0) starts in 10min at 1769350200. oncall: @sre-lead @kevin watching.

deploy-bot: canary started for shard 0. exporting metrics to #deploy-metrics. pinned_version enforced.

kevin: first batch done: 5k rows, cpu on writer 38%, locks transient, replication lag eu-west peaked 8s. so far nominal.

oncall-bot: canary update: 30m elapsed -> errors 0.02%, avg insert time 0.9s, checksum match ok.

sre-lead: green for wave 2 (shard 1+2) but keep shard 3 for last wave due to size. holdpoint remains at post-backfill-check before read-path flip.

marta: note: we will not drop old column until day+2 to allow rollback via feature flag.

product-bot: posted short blurb to release notes draft: https://redwood/release/notes/v2026_03_24 (will update with final metrics).

kevin: final reminder: if we need to revert quickly run the prepared revert on the pinned deploy and then flip feature flag off. revert takes ~15-30m per shard worst-case.

marta: post-run action items: add a runbook section for "json->normalized backfill single-writer" and record why we prefer app-worker parsing to avoid primary CPU spikes.

oncall-bot: canary complete at 1769350280. metrics posted.

deploy-bot: rollout paused awaiting manual approval for wave 3. to continue: comment `continue wave3` in this thread.
